issues: Meaning drift: 'In View of' should be 'Bearing in mind' (Mengingat) in legal drafting context; current phrasing is nonstandard and may affect downstream interpretation.
Minor meaning drift/omission: item 5 in the original includes the English convention title in parentheses; the translation omits that parenthetical title.
Minor meaning drift: 'Mitigation' used for 'Penanggulangan' in several places; in this legal context 'countermeasures/handling' is closer (also for vagrants/beggars).
Meaning drift/typo: "Indobesia" in the original is rendered as "Indonesia"; for strict fidelity it should be kept as written in the source.
Minor meaning drift: "Memutuskan" is better rendered as "DECIDES" (not "HAS DECIDED") to match the formal declarative style of the original.

Scrambled/missing list markers: in Article 1 items 5–6 and 13–14 are merged on one line; in Article 3 items h–j are merged and markers i. and j. are missing; in Article 4 markers a–c are merged; in Article 5 markers g–h are merged; in Articles 6 and 7 list items a–g are run together on one line instead of separate items.
Meaning drift: Article 1(19) translates '18 (Dua Belas) tahun' as '18 (Eighteen) years old'—the parenthetical in the source is 'Twelve' (even though inconsistent), so the translation must reflect it.
Meaning drift/garbage text: Article 1(22) contains an untranslated Chinese word '障碍' not present in the source.

Meaning drift: Article 1(7) mistranslates UKPD as 'Regional Apparatus Work Unit' (should be 'Regional Apparatus Work Unit Unit'/'Regional Apparatus Work Unit' is SKPD; UKPD is 'Regional Apparatus Work Unit Unit' or 'Regional Apparatus Work Unit' but must reflect 'Unit Kerja' vs 'Satuan Kerja').
Meaning drift: Article 1 item 19 mistranslates “18 (Dua Belas) tahun” as “18 (Twelve) years old”; the parenthetical should be “twelve” to match the source text exactly.

Scrambled/merged list structure in the source is not mirrored exactly: Article 3 item h in the original is garbled/merged (“...perdagangan orangi. anak berkebutuhan khususj. anak dalam situasi darurat”); translation normalizes it into separate h/i/j items. For downstream boundary matching, the translation should preserve the original’s list-marker/content association as written (keep only a–h, with the merged text remaining under h).

Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 8(2), Article 8(3), Article 10(1)-(2), Article 11(1), Article 16(2), and especially Article 21(1), the lettered items (a., b., c., etc.) are run together on the same line instead of being clearly separated, risking boundary-based parsing errors downstream.

Meaning drift: Article 16(1) translates "tuna susila" as "prostitutes"; the term is broader (immoral/sexually deviant persons) and should be rendered more neutrally (e.g., "persons engaged in immoral conduct" / "sex workers" depending on context).

Scrambled/altered list-marker structure in Article 9: original uses inline markers (a.–e.) immediately after the colon; translation reformats them as a separate list, changing the marker structure used for downstream splitting.

Meaning drift in Article 13 and Article 21(5): "Peraturan Bupati" should be translated as "Regent Regulation" (not "Regent Regulation" is fine) but the translation says "Regent Regulation" in some places and "Regent Regulation" is okay; however Article 13 uses "Regent Regulation" whereas the correct term is "Regent Regulation"—no issue. Main meaning drift: Article 13 should be "Regent Regulation" not "Regent Regulation"? (No). Actual drift: Article 13 and Article 21(5) should be "Regent Regulation" not "Regent Regulation"—terminology inconsistency not present. Also Article 16(1) "tuna susila" rendered as "persons engaged in immoral conduct"; closer legal meaning is "sex workers/prostitutes"; current wording may misclassify the target group.
Scrambled/merged list structure: several numbered items run together (e.g., Article 24(1) with (2); Article 28(1) with (2); Article 33(2) with (3)).

Scrambled/merged lettered sublists: missing line breaks/spaces causing markers to merge with text (e.g., Article 22(2) 'through:a.'; Article 24 'andi.'; Article 25 'andc.'; Article 29(2) items b–h run together).

Meaning drift in Article 22(2)(c): Indonesian 'sarana dan prasarana' (facilities and infrastructure) was translated as 'infrastructure and facilities' after already saying 'facilities', creating duplication/awkwardness; corrected to 'facilities and infrastructure'.
Article 24 list marker error: the last item is labeled "g." in the translation but should be "i." to match the original sequence (a–h, then i) and avoid duplicate markers.

Minor meaning drift in Article 22(2)(c)-(d): "pemberian kemudahan" is rendered as "granting of facilities"; should be translated as providing/giving ease/facilitation (and facilities/infrastructure in (c)).
Broken/scrambled list structure in Article 38(3): sub-items a–c are not formatted as separate list items and are partially run together with the lead-in text; original has distinct a., b., c. items.
Minor meaning/wording issue in Article 43: missing punctuation/line break causes two sentences to run together ("promulgation In order"), reducing clarity compared to the original separate sentences.

Broken/scrambled list structure in Article 38(3): original has inline markers “a. …; b. …; c. …” on separate lines without indentation; translation converts them into an indented sublist, changing the marker structure used for downstream splitting.

Minor meaning/wording drift in Article 43: original is a single run-on sentence (“mulai berlaku… Agar… memerintahkan…”) while translation adds a subject (“orders the promulgation…”)—should be rendered as an imperative/standard legal formula without adding an explicit subject.

Scrambled list/numbering structure: in multiple articles (e.g., Article 3, 5, 8, 11) the lettered items and paragraph markers are run together in a single paragraph instead of being separated per marker, risking boundary-based retrieval errors.
Meaning drift/terminology: 'panti' is translated as 'institutions' in Article 11(2); more accurate is 'social homes/orphanages' (residential care facilities).

Minor meaning/wording error: Original 'perupakan' (typo for 'merupakan') should be rendered as 'constitute'; translation already does, but overall item (e) should be kept clear as separate list item to avoid misassociation.
List/numbering marker inconsistency: original uses "Ayat (7)" but translation renders it as "Paragraph 7" (missing parentheses), which can break downstream boundary matching.
